message.content:
Christopher Clavius, a leading Jesuit astronomer, argued against Copernican heliocentrism on mathematical and theological grounds.
Tycho Brahe rejected the idea that Earth moves, partly because he saw no stellar parallax.
Many theologians also criticized the model for seeming to contradict Scripture.
Did Clavius oppose the math, the astronomy, or the religious implications?
Why did Brahe find a stationary Earth so compelling?
Was the strongest criticism perhaps the lack of expected observational evidence?
His system faced formidable resistance!
The objections were both scientific and doctrinal!
His ideas nevertheless survived those challenges!
